figures.caption: The incircle and circumcircle share the symmetry center; their radii sum to the width.
figures.alt: Reuleaux triangle with vertex triangle, concentric inscribed and enclosing circles, and labeled radii.

figures.caption: Regular Reuleaux polygons of width one; their areas increase toward the disk.
figures.alt: Three equal-width outlines: Reuleaux triangle, regular pentagon, and regular nonagon.

figures.caption: A perturbed and exactly closed unit-edge pentagram gives unequal boundary arc angles. The support lines remain one unit apart.
figures.alt: Irregular five-arc Reuleaux polygon with labeled vertices, chord polygon, and parallel supporting lines.

figures.caption: Two unit disks centered at ±a on the horizontal axis; here a=1/2.
figures.alt: Lens formed by two overlapping unit disks, with horizontal support lines at heights one and square root of one minus a squared.

figures.caption: Support function h(θ)=1/2+0.045 cos(3θ); curvature radius stays positive.
figures.alt: Rounded threefold constant-width curve with two pairs of parallel supporting lines.

figures.caption: Erosion retains the three disk centers and reduces every disk radius from one to 1−t.
figures.alt: Four nested rounded triangles illustrating increasing erosion distances.

figures.caption: Six equally spaced supporting lines can be chosen at equal distance from a common center.
figures.alt: A width-one Reuleaux triangle inside its circumscribed regular hexagon.

figures.caption: Adding a radius-0.15 disk adds 0.15 to the support function and 0.30 to the width.
figures.alt: Nested smooth constant-width curves representing a body and its outer parallel body.

figures.caption: The midpoints O and H reduce the four cross-distance constraints to h²+u²+v²=1.
figures.alt: Three-dimensional diagram of two perpendicular opposite edges, their midpoints, and four dashed unit cross edges.

figures.caption: Spherical patches are blue, wedges pale green, and spindle patches orange. Both choices have the same exact area and volume. Triangulated illustrations.
figures.alt: Side-by-side rendered Meissner tetrahedra with the star and face choices of smoothed edges.

figures.caption: An auxiliary interior point divides the spherical octant into three geodesic triangles.
figures.alt: Spherical octant with its three coordinate-axis vertices and geodesic spokes from an interior helper point.

figures.caption: Rotate the minor arc AB around its chord; the distance from C to the chord is cos(θ/2).
figures.alt: Unit circle center below a horizontal chord, with two unit radii and the central angle marked.

figures.caption: The skeleton S lies inside P, which lies inside the endpoint-tangent polygon C. Every convex K between S and C has the same reflected mixed area. Both panels have width-one Reuleaux polygons.
figures.alt: Triangle and irregular Reuleaux pentagon, each overlaid with its inner skeleton and outer tangent polygon.

figures.caption: The hull H is a regular hexagon between concentric circles of radii 1/2 and 1/√3. The inner disk belongs to the hull, not necessarily to either Reuleaux triangle.
figures.alt: Two reflected Reuleaux triangles inside their common hexagonal convex hull, with inner and outer concentric circles.

figures.caption: Three translates share only the disk center O. Their tangent sectors have angle 120° and partition the full angle; the curved bodies leave gaps farther from O. Boundary contacts are allowed.
figures.alt: Three differently colored Reuleaux triangles in a unit-radius circle, touching at its center, with three dashed tangent rays and 120-degree angle marks.

figures.caption: Moving each endpoint of a diameter to O gives two translates in the unit disk. They lie on opposite sides of a common supporting line and touch only at O.
figures.alt: Two identical irregular Reuleaux pentagons, translated to touch at the center of a unit circle, with a dashed separating tangent line.

figures.caption: The endpoints and the filled interval have the same convex hull and support function, but different distance functions. Their Hausdorff distance is one, attained by the distance-function gap at x=0.
figures.alt: Graphs of distance to two endpoints and distance to the interval between them; their maximum vertical difference is one at the origin.

figures.caption: Filled dots represent G_n; hollow dots are removed from the open interval Ω_n. As n grows, the compact grids fill [0,1], while the domain clearances shrink uniformly to zero. Removed points are shown with enlarged markers, not positive-length holes.
figures.alt: Three progressively finer grids, the corresponding punctured intervals, and their triangular clearance graphs decreasing in height.

figures.caption: An exact two-vertex Blaschke motion of the regular width-one pentagon. Blue is the initial body, orange the perturbed body. Areas are computed by circular-arc integration; the plot illustrates, rather than proves, the negative second variation.
figures.alt: Initial and deformed Reuleaux pentagons beside a graph of area with a strict local maximum at the undeformed pentagon.

figures.caption: A shortest arc cd (purple) and opposite corner q are replaced using the unit-circle intersection p. The new body has five arcs; c and d become smooth points. Dashed blue is the previous boundary. Both bodies are constructed and checked as width-one Reuleaux polygons.
figures.alt: An irregular seven-arc Reuleaux polygon and its five-arc replacement, with the shortest arc and points a, b, c, d, p, q labeled.

figures.caption: The same Reuleaux triangle inside intersections of 6, 12 and 24 equally spaced supporting half-planes. At a corner several successive support lines can meet at one point, producing zero-length sides in the indexed polygon.
figures.alt: Three increasingly fine circumscribed equiangular supporting polygons around one Reuleaux triangle.

figures.caption: Opposite supports remain one unit apart while the three strips slide. At the endpoint three sides vanish and an equilateral triangle remains. These straight-sided polygons are not constant-width bodies.
figures.alt: A regular hexagon, an alternating-side hexagon, and a limiting equilateral triangle obtained by sliding three strips.

figures.caption: The orange region is removed near q and the purple region is added near p. The line pq splits them into the paired curvilinear pieces used in the comparison lemma. Their boundaries include circular arcs, so straight-triangle areas would give the wrong subtraction. Dashes show the original boundary; the solid gray curve is the replacement.
figures.alt: Two views of the same shortest-arc replacement, with the removed curved cap shaded orange and the added curved cap shaded purple; points p, q, r, s, a, b, c, d are marked.

figures.caption: A piecewise analytic support function for a width-one regular Reuleaux pentagon. Equal intervals alternate between curvature radius zero and one: zero intervals map to single vertices, while unit intervals trace unit-circle arcs. Curvature values at the finitely many jumps are immaterial.
figures.alt: Support and stepwise curvature-radius graphs with equal switching intervals beside the corresponding Reuleaux pentagon, whose vertices are orange and arcs blue.

figures.caption: For N=8 and k=2N+3=19, the two sine modes agree at every grid direction, so all sampled curvature values are 1/2. Between them the candidate curvature is negative on open intervals. This function cannot be the curvature radius of a convex support function despite passing the sampled inequalities.
figures.alt: An oscillating curvature candidate crossing below zero between eight positive sample points; negative regions are shaded.

figures.caption: Adding a horizontal segment of length ℓ extends every nonempty horizontal slice by ℓ. The shaded curved band therefore has area ℓb, where b is the perpendicular width. For a radius-r disk and its diameter segment, ℓ=b=2r, giving mixed area 2r² despite the segment having zero area. Circle arcs are sampled only for rendering.
figures.alt: A disk before and after adding a horizontal segment. In the sum, two horizontal arrows across the added curved band both have length ell; a vertical dimension marks the disk width b.
